title: Atera Pricing: Plans and Cost per Technician (2026)
summary: Atera pricing starts at $129 per technician monthly on annual contracts, up to $249 for month-to-month plans.
body_markdown:
## Connecting Atera to Other Tools with Activepieces


Add Activepieces only when you need to push Atera tickets, alerts or customer records into software Atera has no native connection to, which is where its 750 integrations, counted from the open source monorepo, come in.


It changes neither Atera's per-technician price nor the job of your RMM (remote monitoring and management platform).


Unlike the quote-only vendors, you can settle this one yourself, in an afternoon, before anyone sends a price.


The Free plan on Activepieces Cloud includes 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows, and the Activepieces pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, any number of steps, whereas Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module.


A ticket-to-task flow with ten mapped steps therefore costs the same as one with two.


### When Atera's built-in automation is enough


If the work stays inside Atera, such as routing a ticket, running a script on an alert or notifying a technician, use Atera's own automation.


It's already in the plan you pay for, so every extra tool you bolt on is a second thing to maintain and a second place a client's data can leak or break.


Don't add a workflow layer for something you can do for free where the data already lives.


### When a separate workflow tool earns its place


Only one situation justifies Activepieces, even though unlimited flows come on every plan, including the free one: a client's billing, project or chat tool sits outside Atera and someone is retyping data between the two.


That retyping is unbilled labor, and on a shared setup it quietly gets absorbed by the clients who pay on time.


The handoff stops being a person's job once Activepieces listens for an event in Atera and passes the data to the other tool, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties all run Activepieces in production.


Do the steps in this order, because the first one can stop you before you build anything:


1. Check that your Atera plan includes API and webhook access. If it doesn't, the tier you need is part of the cost of this project, so settle that before you plan the build.
2. Generate your Atera API key from your account settings, and store it somewhere only the people running the automation can read.
3. In Activepieces, build a flow whose trigger is a new ticket or a new alert from Atera.
4. Map the fields to the target tool: ticket title to task name, customer to client record, priority to whatever the other tool calls urgency. Match them by what the receiving person needs to see, not by whatever field happens to share a name.
5. Test with a single ticket, and confirm that exactly one record appears in the target tool with the right customer attached.


Catch a mismapped field on a single test ticket, where it is cheapest to find. If a flow ever sends records to the wrong client, you find out on a test rather than on an invoice.


Once that ticket lands cleanly, you can widen the trigger to cover alerts or more ticket types.
